statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is moderate at 35 as a carried rates, energy and geopolitical condition rather than an equity-structure one.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z on Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly twenty-two hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the rates and energy backdrop. Re-verification during this hour found the Friday close, VIX, the curve and crude unchanged and no new military escalation or Hormuz supply disruption, only continuing diplomatic rhetoric. No danger window is carried, because none can be evidenced in a closed market. The first genuine price-path test falls outside this horizon and is scored by a later assessment.
headline: Third consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, with Friday's cash NDX close of 29,308.86, +0.33%, re-verified as the last observed Nasdaq-100 reference.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which now run into Sunday's first UTC hour. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. That close snapped a five-day Nasdaq-100 losing streak, though the index still ended the week about 2% lower alongside the S&P 500 and the Dow. VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the base of a 14.77-15.95 range. The backdrop behind Stress is unchanged rather than improving: the 2-year closed at 4.24%, the 5-year at 4.43%, the 10-year at 4.74% and the 30-year at 5.28% after a week in which a Treasury buyback expansion produced only a short-lived rally before the long end resumed rising. Crude held its range into the close, with WTI at 87.06, up 0.26%, and Brent at 94.39. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context is aligned with that picture rather than contradicting it, showing modest index gains, a lower volatility future, firmer gold and softer Treasury futures, and it is used here as supporting context only, never as live price-path evidence. Re-verification in this hour found no new military escalation, no Strait of Hormuz closure and no attack on energy infrastructure since the halt; the US-Iran track has produced only sanctions rhetoric and negotiating positions. Nothing in a closed market can establish the persistent one-way structure that Tail measures, so Tail holds a low closed-venue floor while Stress carries the unresolved long-end repricing, the elevated crude complex and weekend gap risk into the Sunday reopen.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is nearly complete: 18 hourly assessments are available and 6 clock-hours, all in the 21 August overnight window, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the early overnight, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, then a step down to 10, 5 and finally 4 as the venue moved into its 21:00Z Friday halt. Stress traced the same arc in reverse scale, easing from the high fifties to 36 by the final available hour as equity-structure risk was replaced by carried rates, energy and weekend gap risk. No danger window was published in any of those hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the horizon ends at 2026-08-23T00:00:00Z, roughly twenty-two hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress eases from 35 to a 34 trough through the deep weekend hours and then drifts back to 40 by the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens; the carry behind it is unchanged, with a 30-year at 5.28% after a nineteen-year high earlier in the week, crude held near 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse now running through economic pressure rather than strikes. Confidence decays from 86 to 74 across the horizon, reflecting distance from the last verified observation rather than any weakness in the evidence gathered. No danger window is published, no US release, auction or Fed appearance falls inside the horizon, and the first genuine price-path test lies beyond it at the Sunday reopen.
